newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST-Polish 1997 GDP seen up 5.3 pct-thinktank.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Polish 1997 GDP seen up 5.3 pct-thinktank.

text.p: Poland's economy should grow by 5.3 percent next year and 5.4 percent in 1998, down from last year's 6.9 percent but up from 1996's forecast of 4.7 percent, an independent think-thank said in a report issued on Thursday.

The private Gdansk Institute for Market Economy Research (IBnGR) said in its quarterly forecast the economy was showing signs of overheating, with domestic demand and imports both up amid the slower 1996 economic growth of about 4.7 percent.

"This year's GDP rise is likely to be lower than what's needed for an economy which wants to catch up with highly developed economies, with about five percent annual growth preferable," the institute's deputy president Jacek Dabrowski told a news conference.
The institute expected Poland's merchandise trade deficit to increase to $6.7 billion this year, $9.6 billion next year and $10.7 billion in 1998 from $1.8 million last year.
It said domestic demand would rise by 8.2 percent this year, 6.9 percent next year and 6.3 percent in 1998 from its 6.5-percent rise last year.

"Domestic demand is growing at about eight percent this year and gross domestic product is growing at 4.7 percent...a difference that could cause price growth pressure," said senior analyst Miroslaw Gronicki, the report's author.

He said the central bank, which said it wanted real interest rates to rise, would likely not cut nominal rates even if inflation fell about two percent points in year-on-year terms from the current 19.5 percent.

But he said exports could increase next year upon a likely weaker zloty and a possible economic turnaround in neighbouring Germany, and said Poland could reverse its trade-deficit trend toward the end of 1998.

Dabrowski said 1996 inflation should end at above 19 percent, above the government target of 17 percent, and that inflation next year would be some 15 percent, above the government's target of 13 percent.
